newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait parliament passes $14 bln 1996/97 budget.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait parliament passes $14 bln 1996/97 budget.

text.p: Kuwait's oppositon-dominated parliament on Tuesday retroactively approved a 4.21 billion dinar ($14 billion) state budget with a forecast net deficit of 1.21 billion dinars for the fiscal year which started July 1.
The budget was passed unanimously by 37 deputies present after a three-hour debate.
Total revenue in the 1996/97 budget was put at three billion dinars, including 2.56 billion dinars in oil earnings.
Oil revenue was calculated at a conservative weighted average price of $13 a barrel, unchanged from the past two years although world prices have been much higher this year.
The world benchmark Brent crude is currently trading in London at $22.65 a barrel. Kuwait has a daily oil output of about two million barrels.
In July the government said it expected to halve the 1.32 billion dinar forecast deficit for the last fiscal year mainly because of the higher oil prices.
The budget passed by parliament forecast a 1995/96 deficit of 1.32 billion dinars and revenues of 2.91 billion dinars.
Actual budget figures for the last fiscal year have not been released yet.
By law 10 percent of total revenues is placed in a special fund for future generations, making the gross projected deficits 1.51 billion dinars for 1996/97 and 1.61 billion dinars for 1995/96.
Deficits are traditionally financed from general reserves in the form of a debt to the future generations fund.
Since the 1990-91 Gulf crisis, Kuwait's foreign investment portfolio has fallen to about $35 billion from over $100 billion. ($1=0.3 dinars)
